name: code-viewer
purpose: Read-only code display with line numbers, syntax highlighting for TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON, HTML, CSS, SQL, Bash, and Markdown (an in-repo tokenizer that produces text nodes with classes, never HTML), highlighted lines, a wrap toggle, a copy button, and a diff view (unified or side by side) computed in the repo with Myers' algorithm. The code is a focusable, named region; files above 400 rows are virtualized on the shared windowing engine.
whenToUse: Showing source code, configuration, JSON exports, or SQL to read and copy.
Reviewing changes between two versions of a text, such as a policy or a configuration file.
Documentation and support pages with copyable snippets.
whenNotToUse: Editing code: use a text area or a dedicated editor.
Short inline code in a sentence: use the Typography Code element.
Rich formatted documents: use Prose or the Rich Text Editor.
responsive: Fills its container; long lines scroll horizontally (line numbers stay pinned) or wrap; the toolbar wraps on narrow containers. The side-by-side diff always wraps its columns.
rtl: The toolbar mirrors with the page direction; the code itself always renders left to right (dir=ltr), as source code is written.
theme: Component tokens for the code background, gutter, line numbers, nine token colors, added, removed, and highlighted line backgrounds, the highlight bar, font size, and radius; every text color is in the contrast gate on the code background and on each line background in every theme.
security: Code is never parsed as HTML: the tokenizer yields plain data and the viewer creates text nodes. The copy button writes plain text through the asynchronous Clipboard API. No network access.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. The text stays in memory for the lifetime of the viewer.

budgets.metric: CodeViewer.create with a 10,000-line TypeScript file (tokenize and first render)
diffLines over two 10,000-line texts with a few changes

performance.testedScale: 10,000 lines (code and diff); up to 100,000 lines. The diff search is capped at 2,000 edits, beyond which the changed middle is shown as one deletion and one insertion.

limitations: A fixed set of languages; embedded scripts and styles inside HTML are shown as plain text.
Regular expression literals in JavaScript are not highlighted.
The side-by-side diff always wraps long lines.
unsupported: Editing, folding, search inside the code, and word-level diff highlighting.
antiPatterns: Putting secrets in displayed code: the copy button and the DOM expose the full text.
Relying on token colors to convey meaning: diff lines carry Added and Removed text for screen readers, but highlighting is decoration.
